content:
Bloomberg yesterday reported that Apple is about to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" rental contract to replace the existing iPhone Upgrade Program.

There appear to be two major differences between the two, one of which may be quite worrying...

The iPhone Upgrade Program mechanism is simple and straightforward. Your purchase cost is spread over 24 monthly installments, and once the two-year contract expires, you fully own the device, with zero interest on the credit.

(In addition, you can choose to upgrade to a new iPhone after 12 months. In this case, a new two-year contract begins, and you essentially sell the old device back to Apple for the installments you have already paid.)

Apple has yet to make any official announcement about the new replacement plan, so for now we cannot know exactly how the new plan will operate. However, Bloomberg says the new plan will cover most other Apple products, with a three-year purchase term for the Mac. So far, that still sounds like good news.

But what is concerning is that the report hints the new plan will operate very much like an auto lease. Under such contracts, you do not repay the full cost of the product during the lease term. Instead, your monthly payments only cover the depreciation of the product during the lease term, plus any interest charges. When the lease expires, you do not own the product — you are essentially just renting it the whole time.

Similarly, assuming it truly works the same way as an auto lease, at the end of the lease you either return the product or pay a "balloon payment" — the difference between the depreciation amount and the product's full price.

Of course, this means the monthly payments will be lower than the current plan. You can think of it this way: lower monthly payments are a good thing, because they make Apple products affordable for more people.

However, what is worrying is that most people will not set aside an extra sum each month to cover the balloon payment when the lease ends. The most common situation with auto leases is that people return the car at the end of the lease and then sign a new lease for a new car. Ultimately, they are trapped in a never-ending cycle, and will never truly own the product.

If the new Apple upgrade plan works the same way, the same situation will occur. People who buy this way will essentially be forced to upgrade their iPhone every two years and their Mac every three years, rather than being able to choose to keep using their phone for a few more years. Even ignoring interest entirely, the total cost of ownership over the long run will increase significantly.

In addition, if the report that AppleCare+ is not included turns out to be true, users may encounter situations during the lease term where the device is lost, stolen, or so badly damaged it cannot be repaired. Not only will they have to keep paying monthly installments for a device they no longer have, they will also have to pay the balloon payment at the end of the lease.

I understand that Apple wants to simplify its operations by offering a single upgrade plan and therefore retiring the existing one. But I think it would be better for consumers to be given a choice of plans, so that everyone can enjoy the credit benefits while still deciding for themselves how often to upgrade.

What do you think about this? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
